When Allah loves someone, Gabriel and heaven love him and earth accepts him; faith's sweetness lies in loving others for Allah's sake and holding Allah and His Apostle dearest.
The Prophet forbade laughing at someone who passes wind, and asked how a man can beat his wife like a stallion camel and then embrace her.
A Muslim's blood, property and honour are sacred; abusing him is evil-doing, cursing him like murder, and calling him a disbeliever falsely rebounds; the Prophet himself never abused anyone.
When two men abused each other and one's face swelled with anger, the Prophet said seeking refuge with Allah from Satan would calm him, but the man refused.
The Prophet came to tell the date of the Night of Qadr, but two men quarrelled and its knowledge was taken away; seek it on the ninth, seventh or fifth.
Told that insulting a man's mother showed traits of ignorance, Abu Dhar dressed his slave as himself, for slaves are brothers to be fed and clothed as oneself.
After the Prophet ended Zuhr at two rak'at, Dhul-Yadain, the long-armed, asked if he forgot; when the people confirmed it, he prayed two more and two prostrations of forgetfulness.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said one man was punished for not guarding against his urine and the other for spreading calumnies, and planted a split palm leaf on each.
The Prophet said the best family among the Ansar is the Banu An-Najjar.
The Prophet called a man evil before admitting him, then spoke to him politely, saying the worst people are those others avoid for fear of their foul tongue or wrongdoing.
In Medina's graveyard the Prophet heard two people punished in their graves, one for urine and one for calumnies, and placed half a green palm leaf on each grave.
The Prophet said a Qattat will not enter Paradise.
Whoever does not give up false statements, evil deeds and bad words, Allah has no need of his leaving food and drink in fasting.
The worst people before Allah on Resurrection Day are the double-faced, who show one face to some people and another face to others.
Told that an Ansari said a distribution was not meant to please Allah, the Prophet's face changed with anger, and he said Moses was hurt worse yet stayed patient.
The Prophet rebuked men who over-praised another, saying they had cut his back or neck; one who must praise should say 'I think', for none can sanctify anyone before Allah.
Abu Bakr said his waist sheet slackened on one side, and the Prophet said he was not among those who drag their garments out of pride.
Lubaid bin Asam worked magic on the Prophet with a comb and hair hidden in Dharwan's well; Allah revealed it and cured him, and he would not spread the evil.
Beware of suspicion, the worst of false tales; do not spy, seek faults, be jealous, hate or desert one another beyond three days, but be brothers, O Allah's worshippers.
The Prophet told Aisha he did not think two certain men knew anything of their religion, and Al-Laith said the two were hypocrites.
All sins are forgiven except those whose doers expose what Allah screened, and on the Day Allah will make a believer confess his sins, then forgive what He had screened.
The people of Paradise are the obscure and humble, whose oaths by Allah He fulfils, and the people of the Fire are the cruel, violent, proud and conceited.
Any slave girl of Medina could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever she wished, Anas said.
Aisha broke her vow never to speak to Ibn Az-Zubair, freeing forty slaves, as a Muslim may not desert his brother over three nights; the better greets first.
The Prophet knew Aisha's moods: pleased, she swore by the Lord of Muhammad, and angry, by the Lord of Abraham, leaving only his name, she said.
The Prophet visited Abu Bakr's house morning and evening, and one day came at noon to say he had been allowed to migrate.
The Prophet ate with an Ansari household, prayed in their house on a mat sprinkled with water, and invoked Allah's blessing on his hosts.
Umar urged the Prophet to buy a silk cloak for delegations; he said silk is worn by one with no share hereafter, then sent Umar a cloak only to sell.
The Prophet made Abdur-Rahman and Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' brothers, told Abdur-Rahman to give a wedding feast, and made a brotherhood pact between the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's home.
The Prophet smiled rather than laughing aloud: at Rifa'a's divorced wife, women hiding from Umar, a poor man's Ramadan offence, a rough bedouin, Jarir, and rain prayers.
Truthfulness leads to righteousness and Paradise, and lying to wickedness and the Fire, until a man is written before Allah as truthful or as a liar.
The signs of a hypocrite are three: he lies when he speaks, breaks his promises, and betrays what he is entrusted with.
In a dream the Prophet was shown a man whose cheek was being torn, a liar whose lies spread over the world, punished so until the Day of Resurrection.
Hudhaifa said Ibn Um Abd most resembled the Prophet in bearing, piety and calm from leaving his house till returning, though none knew him alone with his family.
Abdullah said the best talk is Allah's Book and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad.
None is more patient than Allah with those ascribing children to Him, yet He provides for them; angered by an Ansari's remark, the Prophet recalled Moses, harmed worse yet patient.
The Prophet censured people who avoided something he did and allowed, saying he knew Allah better than they and feared Him more.
The Prophet was shyer than a virgin in her room, and when he disliked something it showed on his face.
Calling one's brother a disbeliever makes one of them so; cursing a believer or calling him a disbeliever is like killing him, and suicide is punished by its own means.
When Mu'adh called a man a hypocrite for leaving his long Surat al-Baqara prayer, the Prophet rebuked Mu'adh for burdening people and told him to recite shorter surahs.
